rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract rather than tuned from data. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the axle at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m (10 mm spacing, which is narrower than the 25 mm tape so the tape always covers at least two sensors), mounted 0.03 m ahead of the axle, with 12 mm footprints. Track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg, all mid-range for stable yaw response. Controller: sensor weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 give a signal that is roughly proportional to lateral error with sign set so a positive signal steers left. kp = 3 gives about 2100 PWM of wheel differential per unit of signal, which is firm but not saturating for small offsets. kd = 0.3 damps the response and ki = 0.05 is kept small to avoid integral windup on bends. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80% of full PWM) is aimed at the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish under 3 s while leaving margin for the bends. line_loss = last_direction so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The main uncertainties are whether 1.6 base speed is fast enough to finish in time and whether kp is too high or low. The next race should show completion_time and steering_oscillation, which will decide whether to raise base_speed or adjust kp and kd.
